sections.title: Saying What You Have
sections.content: 'Tener' means to have. It is irregular twice over: the yo form is 'tengo', and the e of the stem becomes ie in the forms that stress it — the same change you met in 'querer'. Spanish also uses 'tener' where English uses 'to be': 'tengo suerte' is I'm lucky, literally I have luck.

items.english: Do you have any brothers or sisters?

items.spanish: Mi familia saluda a Meg y entiende algunas palabras.
items.english: My family greets Meg and understands a few words.

sections.content: Spanish drops the article when 'tener' means having some of something: '¿Tienes hermanos?', not '¿Tienes unos hermanos?'. Put a number or 'un' back in when you are counting: 'Tengo dos hermanos.'
